title: Bridging evidence gaps in opioid-sparing postoperative pain control for percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a network meta-analysis identifying optimal strategies.
evidence_quotes: Non-opioid analgesics (NSAIDs/paracetamol) showed superior efficacy; opioids excelled short-term but not long-term.

IV paracetamol plus LI-levobupivacaine ranked highest in the multicriteria analysis, although the benefit-risk ranking should be interpreted cautiously because the safety component was based on sparse and imprecise data.
Comparative safety could not be established because complication data were sparse and estimates were highly imprecise.
reason: Acetaminophen, named as paracetamol, is an evaluated analgesic intervention with reported postoperative efficacy outcomes. Its combination with local-infiltration levobupivacaine also receives an explicit outcome ranking. This is direct evidence, although the combination result does not isolate acetaminophen's contribution and comparative safety remains uncertain.

title: Low pressure (8 mmHg) pneumoperitoneum does not significantly reduce postoperative visual analog scale score after laparoscopic cholecystectomy: Randomized trial.
evidence_quotes: Patients scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) were randomized into two groups: LPP group (8 mmHg) versus SPP group (14 mmHg).
Secondary outcomes included operative time, analgesic consumption, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), and surgical complications.
However, the mean consumption of paracetamol during the first 24 hours was significantly lower in the LPP group compared to the SPP group (1.04 ± 0.906 vs. 1.35 ± 0.873; p = 0.014).
reason: Paracetamol is acetaminophen, but its consumption is measured as an outcome of pneumoperitoneum pressure. It is not an evaluated intervention or comparator, and the study does not assess outcomes attributable to acetaminophen treatment.

title: Feeding following cleft palate surgery: a prospective randomized clinical trial comparing suprazygomatic maxillary nerve block and greater palatine nerve block.
evidence_quotes: Children 1-10 years of age undergoing palate surgery were randomized to either SZMNB or GPNB.
Secondary aims were postoperative pain scores and need for rescue paracetamol administration (pain score >4).
Group SZMNB did also show lower pain scores during 0-12 hour postoperatively (p<0.05-0.001) and fewer patients needed rescue paracetamol (p<0.05) compared with the GPNB group.
reason: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) was used only as rescue medication. The trial evaluated two nerve-block techniques; rescue medication use was an outcome of those techniques, not an evaluation of acetaminophen's effects.

title: Nebivolol treatment improves hypertension-induced endothelial cell dysfunction by reducing TGF-β1-dependent senescence and normalizing mitochondrial indices.
evidence_quotes: This study involved 71 patients with newly diagnosed HT, who were randomly assigned to one of three groups based on the antihypertensive treatment: amlodipine, nebivolol, or perindopril.
Serum samples collected before and 6 weeks after treatment were applied to ECs in vitro to assess their angiogenic activity, cellular senescence, mitochondrial metabolism, and oxidative stress.
Results showed that exposure of ECs to serum from patients treated for 6 weeks significantly altered EC function, with varying effects among the drugs.
reason: Amlodipine is an explicitly evaluated randomized comparator, not an incidental mention. The study measures endothelial-cell responses to serum collected before and after treatment across the drug groups. This provides comparator evidence for amlodipine, although the abstract emphasizes nebivolol and does not report amlodipine-specific effect estimates.

title: Efficacy and Safety Profile of a Triple Single-Pill Combination of Valsartan/Amlodipine/Chlorthalidone in Patients with Uncontrolled Hypertension.
evidence_quotes: Patients (n = 294) with inadequately controlled hypertension after a 4-week run-in phase with valsartan/amlodipine (80/5 mg) were randomized to receive KDF1901 (valsartan/amlodipine/chlorthalidone 160/10/25 mg, n = 147) or KDF1901-R (valsartan/amlodipine 160/10 mg, n = 147) for 8 weeks.
At week 8, the KDF1901 group exhibited a significantly greater reduction in MSSBP (-22.8 ± 1.0 mmHg) compared with the dual therapy group (-16.7 ± 1.0 mmHg, P < 0.0001).
Overall, the incidence of TEAEs was similar between groups (24.7% vs 21.5%, P = 0.5783), with mild cases of dizziness were most commonly reported.
reason: Amlodipine is an explicit component of both randomized treatment regimens, with measured blood-pressure and safety outcomes. This is direct evidence about amlodipine-containing combination therapy, not an incidental mention. Because both arms contain the same amlodipine dose, the trial does not isolate amlodipine’s individual contribution.
